segments.t: Stunned by Ainura's revelation, Vika pieces together the truth about the Halloween prank that nearly got her fired. German himself locked Nagiyev in the coffin just so he could play the hero and win Vika's heart. Let's listen to Vika's furious reaction and Denis's new tough-guy act in Russian.
Только смотри не потеряй этот ключ.
Не волнуйтесь, ключ только у меня.
Значит, это всё подстроил сам Герман!
Какой же он хитрый подлец!
Вот такой он красивый человек.
Вика, он за всё ответит.
Я тебе это твёрдо обещаю.
И я тоже хочу помочь.
Сегодня мы ужинаем у Сени дома.
Но у меня планы на вечер.
Правильно, ты идёшь со мной к Сене.
Мы встретимся вечером после работы.
Now let's examine how Vika joins Barinov's conspiracy and Denis tests Senya's advice line by line.
Только смотри не потеряй этот ключ.

'Just make sure you do not lose that key.' Putting the short word for 'not' right in front of the action word is all Russian needs to make a sentence negative, with no extra helper words like 'do' or 'did'.
Не волнуйтесь, ключ только у меня.
'Do not worry, only I have the key.' Russians say 'by me' or 'with us' where English says 'I have' or 'we have', without needing a separate word for 'have'.
Значит, это всё подстроил сам Герман!
'So German himself set all of this up!' Spoken Russian keeps this brief and expressive, built right around 'engineered, set up' without extra helper words.
Какой же он хитрый подлец!
'What a cunning scoundrel he is!' Here Vika anchors the thought on 'clever, cunning' and finishes on 'scoundrel, villain', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Вот такой он красивый человек.
'That is the kind of handsome man he is.' In everyday Russian, 'neat, handsome' flows straight into 'man' without extra linking words.
Вика, он за всё ответит.
'Vika, he will pay for everything.' Chef Barinov centers this short reply on 'will answer', letting a few direct words carry the whole meaning.
Я тебе это твёрдо обещаю.
'I firmly promise you that.' Spoken Russian keeps this brief and expressive, built right around 'promise' without extra helper words.
И я тоже хочу помочь.
'And I want to help too.' Here Vika anchors the thought on 'also, too' and finishes on 'to help', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Сегодня мы ужинаем у Сени дома.
'Tonight we are having dinner at Senya's place.' Meanwhile, Denis tries out Senya's macho advice by announcing their evening plans as a fact.
Но у меня планы на вечер.
'But I have plans for the evening.' Russians say 'by me' or 'with us' where English says 'I have' or 'we have', without needing a separate word for 'have'.
Правильно, ты идёшь со мной к Сене.
'That's right, you are going with me to Senya's.' Denis overrides her objection with a present-tense verb of motion used for a decided future action.
Мы встретимся вечером после работы.
'We will meet in the evening after work.' He walks off without waiting for an answer, leaving a stunned pause behind him. Let's hear the entire scene in the kitchen again from start to finish.

Но у меня планы на вечер.

With Vika now eager for payback, Viktor Petrovich finally has the perfect bait to trap German. Notice the future verb meaning will answer for and the noun meaning plans. Until next time!
Всего хорошего!
